question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away this kaula teaching?
premises: One might possess vast accumulated wealth
That wealth could fill the ocean with jewels
Such wealth is posed as a comparison
inference: Even wealth enough to fill the ocean with jewels is not a sufficient price.
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a fused and irregular form; parsing is tentative
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation of wealth enough to fill the ocean with jewels...
